confirmed.title: LLM-phase decision waits for the whole round: the streaming queue is closed only by the feed, so a sample-0 passer cannot be committed (and losers cannot be cancelled) until the slowest sample lands or hits its deadline
confirmed.scenario: QuixBugs class, seeds fail at the top site -> release() fires samples 1..3. Sample 0 lands at ~3 s with a candidate that passes the goal subset and the full suite. runQueue's 8 workers all end up in `await queue.next()` (runner.ts:715) because the goal queue is in streaming mode; the only `q.close()` is in feed()'s finally (subgoal.ts:1220), reached when `round.next()` returns null, i.e. when every fired sample has settled. One sample stalls to the 20 s deadline (measured p90 24-37 s; 30 s on repository class) -> runQueue returns ~17 s later than necessary, decideBatch/guard run only then, and all N samples are billed in full. The §4.2/§6.2 'cancelled the moment the guard commits' rule is unreachable in the LLM phase (only the seed-passer grace path ever cancels losers); every LLM-phase step pays the round's full wall.
confirmed.fix: Let the streaming loop end early on a decisive outcome: in runLlmStreaming observe outcomes as they land (e.g. pass an onOutcome hook to runQueue or poll `results` between arrivals) and, when a plausible passer with a completed full-suite run exists, `await round.cancel('commit')` + `q.close()` so the blocked workers return and decideBatch runs; alternatively make runQueue return in streaming mode as soon as `passers >= 1` and let the controller decide, re-entering the stream only when the guard held/continued.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading the code and by a /tmp reproduction against the real runQueue + real VerifyQueue and against the real runLlmStreaming via searchSubGoal. In the SIEVE/streaming LLM phase (QuixBugs/ladder class, t_run <= 2 s) the goal queue is closed only by feed()'s finally at src/synth/search/subgoal.ts:1220, reached when round.next() returns null, i.e. when every fired sample has settled (llm.ts:181-206; source.ts:310-311 "null when it has ended (every started sample settled)"). runQueue's workers block in `await queue.next()` (runner.ts:715) whenever the queue is momentarily empty; queue.ts:504-507 releases them only on close(). stopDispatch (runner.ts:541-542) has no "a passer exists" condition: only passers >= MAX_FULL_SUITE_RUNS_PER_STEP (5, :73), which an LLM round of SAMPLES_PER_ROUND.quixbugs = 4 (source.ts:40) cannot reach alone. So a sample-0 passer classified at ~3 s sits in `results` until the slowest sample lands or hits its 10-20 s deadline (source.ts:37); decideBatch/guard run only then (subgoal.ts:1239), and by then `round.closed()` is true so the cancel at :1234 and settleLlm's cancel('commit') at :1251 are both no-ops: no loser is ever cancelled and all N samples are billed. Repro: (A) real runQueue with a streaming VerifyQueue holding one plausible job: lane classified the passer at +7 ms, runQueue returned at +1504 ms, only when close() fired, passersThisStep=1. (B) real searchSubGoal, scripted round with sample 0 = passer at 5 ms and sample 1 landing at 1500 ms: passer classified +6 ms, decide called +1503 ms, the loser sample still got a lane run, llm.rec.cancelled = [] and trace.llm.cancelled = 0. Qualifier: this is specific to the streaming path; in RANK mode (collectForRank, N-1 or deadline) settleLlm's cancel('commit') does reach the last sample (existing test subgoal-llm.test.ts:356). The wait-for-round-end is partly by design (runLlmStreaming docstring "one decision over everything that ran"; LLM-JEV-DESIGN §4.8 "until the source closes the queue at round end"), but it contradicts §4.2 ("cancelled the moment the guard commits") and §6.2 ("1 cluster -> commit its representative at once") for this path, and the cost (wall = straggler latency up to the 20 s deadline per LLM-phase step, every sample metered in full) is real. Nothing in the loop even lets the wall stop (`wallLeft() < minRunWallMs`) release a worker already parked in next(). DESIGN §22.9/§22.10 do not record this as a known deviation or open item.

confirmed.title: revertDue only fires on a lower `passed` count; a claiming run that fails the committed goal test without lowering the total is never detected, and the lane's green run is adopted as the baseline anyway
confirmed.scenario: The lane's full-suite run passed goal test test_x (ordering-dependent/flaky, or an environment difference between the worktree lane and the workspace). The engine's claiming run on the same tree fails test_x while another previously-failing test happens to pass, so `engineRun.passed === before + 1` and neither `engineDisagreed` nor `baselineRegressed` is true. adoptableLaneRun (index.ts:1053) has already installed the lane's green run as mem.baseline (tree matches by content), so the ledger keeps the goal `fixed`. isCompleteByFact is false (failed > 0); next step engineNeedsRun is false, every goal reads fixed -> proposeDone -> refused (verifiedDone false, Q20) three times -> replan exit. The workspace keeps a patch whose goal test fails and the goal is never re-opened. The design's second trigger ('a goal test in the last commit's evidence.newlyPassing fails in the engine's parsed run') is not implemented.
confirmed.fix: In revertDue also compare the engine's parsed failing ids (mem.lastEngineRun) with `commit.evidence.newlyPassing ∩ goal.tests`; when a goal test fails there, re-open the goal (and emit the revert or at least re-localise from the workspace failure). In rebaseline, refuse the lane-run adoption when mem.lastEngineRun is newer than the commit and disagrees on the goal tests; fall back to running the baseline.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading the code and by a unit-test reproduction run from /tmp against the repo (no repo edits). `revertDue` (src/synth/search/index.ts:997-999) fires only on a count comparison — `engineRun.passed < before` or the synthesizer's own fresh baseline `passed < before` — and `adoptableLaneRun` (index.ts:1053-1068) installs the lane's green full run as `mem.baseline` whenever the loaded tree equals the lane's post-image, without consulting `mem.lastEngineRun`. Because the adopted baseline is green, `reconcile` gets an empty fresh clustering and every prior goal comes back `fixed` (goals.ts inheritGoalState, the trailing `status: 'fixed'` push). When the engine's claiming run on that same tree fails the goal test but its `passed` is >= the pre-patch count, nothing re-opens the goal: no revert, no re-baseline, no re-localisation, and the workspace keeps the patch. The design's second trigger (docs/LLM-JEV-DESIGN.md:276, "a goal test in the last commit's evidence.newlyPassing fails in the engine's parsed run") is not implemented — and cannot be from the data as plumbed: the engine's parsed run reaches the synthesizer as counts only (`JudgeTests` at src/core/types.ts:344-347 has `passed/failed/errors/allPassed`, no ids; `observeWindow` at index.ts:216-219 records only counts into `mem.lastEngineRun`). One correction to the finding's downstream trajectory: it does NOT end in `done` refused three times. `proposeDone('green')` (proposal.ts:778-790) finds `doneReadiness` blocked by "the last executed run shows N passed, 1 failed, 0 errors" and returns the full-suite `run` again, so the synthesizer re-proposes the same claiming run every step (never `done`, never a revert) until the engine's loop detector / step budget ends the run. End state is as the finding says: goal never re-opened, patch left in place. Contrast case: when the tree does not match the lane (no adoption), the synthesizer's own run feeds `reconcile`, which re-opens the goal even though passed > before — so the defect is specifically the adoption path bypassing the ledger's self-correction. Severity medium is right; the premise (a test that passes in the worktree lane but fails in the workspace run — flaky/ordering-dependent or env difference) is external nondeterminism, but the code path is deterministic given it.
verdict.evidence:
Reproduction: /tmp/jev-repro/revert-due.test.ts (run with `npx vitest run --root /tmp/jev-repro --config /tmp/jev-repro/vitest.config.mts revert-due` from the repo; 3/3 pass). Harness mirrors test/unit/synth/search/controller-llm.test.ts (llmJev: true, scripted deps, real LedgerSieveSynthesizer).

Step 3 window = [executedPatch(1), executedRun(2, 'python3 -m pytest -q', {passed:1, failed:1})] → output: `A step3: run | run the full test suite | ['the last executed run shows 1 passed, 1 failed, 0 errors'] | goals g1:fixed[tests/test_gcd.py::test_gcd]`; no 'revert' event; mem.committed length 1. Step 4 with a second identical engine run → `A step4: run | run the full test suite | goals g1:fixed[...]`; runTests calls total 1, searchSubGoal calls total 1.

Case B (before+1, the finding's exact shape): pre-patch failing [test_gcd, test_y], passing [test_other] (before=1); lane green (3 pass) adopted; after step 2 `g1:fixed g2:fixed`; step 3 engine run {passed:2, failed:1} → `B step3: run | run the full test suite | ['the last executed run shows 2 passed, 1 failed, 0 errors'] | goals g1:fixed g2:fixed`; no revert; runTests total 1.

Case C (contrast, no adoption): tree loads as buggy again → synthesizer re-runs the suite (scripted post-patch run: failing [test_gcd], passing [test_other, test_y], passed 2 > before 1) → `C step2: ... goals g1:open[tests/test_gcd.py::test_gcd] g2:fixed[...]`, runTests total 2, no revert (count trigger also silent here) but the goal is re-opened by reconcile.

Code anchors: src/synth/search/index.ts:997 (`engineDisagreed = ... engineRun.passed < before`), :999 (`baselineRegressed` count-only), :1053-1068 (`adoptableLaneRun` — tree-content match only, no check of mem.lastEngineRun), :216-219 (`observeWindow` stores counts only), :636-647 (rebaseline skipped when workspace unchanged; revertDue after), :671 (`engineNeedsRun` false once the engine ran after the change), :720-726 (`allPass(baseline)` → proposeDone 'green'); src/synth/search/proposal.ts:631-650 (`doneReadiness` blocks on failed>0), :778-790 (blocked → `proposeRun` full suite again); src/synth/search/goals.ts inheritGoalState (fresh clusters overlapping a prior come back `open`; priors with no still-failing test are pushed `fixed`); src/core/types.ts:344-347 (`JudgeTests` parsed variant carries no failing ids); docs/LLM-JEV-DESIGN.md:276 (second trigger text). Fix direction consistent with the data available today: in `rebaseline`, refuse `adoptableLaneRun` when `mem.lastEngineRun` is newer than `scratch.lastCommit.step` and shows failed+errors>0 (or, once adopted, drop `scratch.baselineStep` when a later engine full-suite run disagrees with a green baseline) so the synthesizer re-runs the suite and `reconcile` re-opens the goal; implementing the design's id-based trigger additionally requires plumbing the engine's failing ids into `JudgeTests`/`WindowEntry`.

confirmed.title: L2 reproduction scripts (LLM-written, untrusted) execute with cwd = workspace root under a profile that allows workspace writes; no code check rejects file writes, and each script runs 2x at base plus at every rebaseline
confirmed.scenario: writeReproduction -> runRepro(input.run, chunks, {workspace: root}) runs `python ... <script>` through sandboxRunFn with cwd = ctx.workspaceInfo.root; seatbelt allows writes under the workspace (that is how tests run). scriptProblems (repro.ts:122) rejects sys.exit/input/subprocess only. GLM writes a Django repro that does `open('settings_repro.py','w')` or `Path('app/models.py').write_text(...)` to set the scenario up -> the real workspace is modified before any patch. Lanes are git worktrees of HEAD and do not contain the write, so the synthesizer's workspace baseline/repro and the lane runs diverge: spurious `workspace_disagreed` reverts, or a claiming run and `completion.repro = 'pass'` declared on a workspace containing an LLM-written file the evaluator's tree lacks; stage-0 `git status` shows the dirt every step. The design's 'no network, no files' is only a prompt rule here.
confirmed.fix: Run the base/confirmation runs of candidate scripts in a lane (worktree or cp -R scratch) rather than the workspace; extend scriptProblems to reject write-mode `open(`, os.remove/unlink/rename/makedirs, shutil.*, pathlib write_text/write_bytes/mkdir/unlink; and after each base run compare `git status --porcelain` (or the sandbox's changed-file list) with the pre-run state and reject the script when anything changed.

verdict.reason: The premise and the core failure are real and reproduced: an LLM-written L2 script runs with cwd = the real workspace root under a seatbelt profile that explicitly allows file-write* under the workspace; scriptProblems rejects only sys.exit/exit/quit/os._exit, input(, subprocess/os.system and empty/too-long scripts, so a script that does Path(...).write_text(...) into the workspace (new file or overwrite of a tracked source file) is accepted, runs twice at base, passes every survivor filter as a "valid failing reproduction", and the picked script re-runs in the workspace at every rebaseline. Nothing snapshots or compares git status around the runs, so the modification persists. Two of the finding's downstream clauses are inaccurate, though: (1) lanes normally DO contain the write (lanes.ts dirtySnapshot is taken at the lazy createLanes, which happens after the establishing step's L2, and replays tracked+untracked dirt after every reset; only a >200-entry dirty tree drops untracked files), and revertDue/workspace_disagreed compares suite pass counts, not the repro, so "spurious workspace_disagreed reverts" is not the mechanism; (2) an llm_valid/llm_weak oracle can never declare completion (COMPLETING_ORACLE_OUTCOMES = valid/valid_weak/weak_network; complete.ts completionEvidenceHolds). The accurate (and worse) consequence is that the ungated LLM-written file/overwrite becomes the workspace state the search edits (loadFiles/committedBase), is replayed into every lane, and ships in model_patch via `git add -A -N && git diff --binary <base> -- . ':(exclude).jevcode*'` (only .jevcode* excluded), i.e. an LLM edit to a tracked source file reaches the evaluator without passing through any candidate/verification gate. The same exposure exists for reporter-authored snippets on the code-oracle path (oracle/search.ts:340,364), so a fix at the runRepro-caller level (scratch cwd + pre/post porcelain compare) covers both.

confirmed.title: Q18 single-survivor Choice is a consumed 0.5 cut that overrides the absolute Noul
confirmed.scenario: N=3 samples, code checks leave one survivor (the common case: dedupe, quote-anchoring, base-run rejects). The Choice `reproduction` then has options {script_k, none_of_these}, so `pEscape > pTop` is exactly `pEscape > 0.5`. Jev answers Choice {script_0: 0.45, none_of_these: 0.55} but Noul reproduces_issue_script_0 = 0.85 -> readQ18 returns `llm_none` before the Noul thresholds (0.7/0.3) are ever consulted; search/index.ts:1274 drops the ReproGoal and the run proceeds on the best-guess path with no oracle. DESIGN.md §5.4 rule 6 forbids a consumed 0.5 threshold on a borderline single-item judgment, and REPORT §10 says a Choice is relative while the Noul is the absolute answer; here the relative question pre-empts the absolute one.
confirmed.fix: When exactly one script survives, skip the Choice (as guard.ts adviseLonePasser does: 'one option is not a choice') and decide on the Noul alone; with ≥ 2 survivors, use the escape only as a tiebreak/routing signal and let the picked script's Noul (0.7/0.3) decide `llm_valid`/`llm_weak`/none.

verdict.reason: The scenario happens exactly as written. src/synth/llm/repro.ts:204 `if (pEscape > pTop) return none(...)` runs before the Noul thresholds at :211-214, and with a single survivor the Q18 Choice has exactly two options (script_k + none_of_these, built at :150-157 and validated to sum to 1 ± 0.05 by src/jev/validate.ts:77), so the gate is a de-facto 0.5 cut on one item. A temp tsx reproduction against the real readQ18 confirmed: one survivor, Choice {script_0: 0.45, none_of_these: 0.55}, Noul reproduces_issue_script_0 = 0.85 -> outcome `llm_none`, key null, reason "Jev put 0.55 on none_of_these against 0.45 for the best script"; flipping the Choice by 0.10 to {0.55, 0.45} with the identical Noul 0.85 -> `llm_valid`. writeReproduction then returns `done('llm_none', pick, ...)` with goal null (:398, :406) and src/synth/search/index.ts:1274 `written.outcome !== 'llm_none'` fails, so `repositoryGoal(..., null, [])` falls back to `bestGuessTestId` — the run proceeds with no oracle despite a script the design's own threshold calls valid. This is not merely the code deviating from the design: DESIGN.md:3072 and LLM-JEV-DESIGN.md:234 do prescribe "escape > top -> no oracle", but DESIGN.md:3085 simultaneously claims "no consumed decision sits at 0.5 — the Q17/Q18 cuts (0.10 margin, 0.3, 0.7, 0.05 tie)", omitting the implicit 0.5 in the one-survivor escape rule, and §5.4 rule 6 (DESIGN.md:601-609) lists only two sanctioned 0.5 cuts, neither of which this is (it decides whether an oracle exists, not "which non-executing decision is taken"). Rule 3 (:584-587, REPORT §10) says the Choice is relative and the Noul absolute; here the relative answer pre-empts the absolute one. Q18 is also the outlier among its siblings: Q15 (guard.ts:550-552) uses escape only as `suspect = pEscape >= 0.5 && maxNoul < 0.1` and picks by argmax + a 0.3/0.7 Noul override (:558-566); Q17 (rank.ts:253-257) treats escape alone as at most a `weak` signal, `strong` only when the Noul agrees; the Q16 lone passer (guard.ts:572-582) asks a Noul alone "no Choice: one option is not a choice". No unit test covers escape > top (test/unit/synth/llm/repro.test.ts:83-96 does show a single survivor reaching Q18 with a two-option Choice at {0.8, 0.2}). Consequence is a false-negative oracle (the L2 round ≈ $0.0024 + two base runs is spent and discarded), not a false completion — `llm_*` never completes a run — so medium severity is appropriate. The reproduction also showed the multi-survivor variant (two scripts at 0.30/0.30, escape 0.40, both Nouls 0.90 -> `llm_none`), so the proposed fix's second clause (escape as tiebreak/routing, Noul decides) is also warranted.

confirmed.title: Q18 Nouls reuse block-extraction criteria that do not describe what an LLM-written script must satisfy
confirmed.scenario: The consumed quantity (`reproduces_issue_<k>` ≥ 0.7 -> `llm_valid`) is judged against REPRODUCTION_CRITERIA (src/synth/oracle/questions.ts:41-50), written for blocks pasted in an issue: true = 'Python code or a REPL transcript that ... shows the wrong behaviour'; false examples = `pip list`, a traceback, 'the fix the reporter proposes'. None of the false side can apply to a script the code already ran and saw raise, and the true side omits the one property code cannot check: the assertion must be satisfiable once the bug is fixed. An LLM script asserting an over-specific outcome (exact repr/message text the fix need not produce) raises at base, survives every code check, and Jev — applying criteria that only ask 'runnable code showing the wrong behaviour' — scores it 0.8 -> `llm_valid` goal. No correct patch passes it; L1′ feedback then pushes the LLM toward special-casing the script's expectation, and the resulting 'passer' is committed to disk as the honest partial. The design itself flags Q18 accuracy on LLM prose as unmeasured; the criteria mismatch makes the measured 18/23 basis inapplicable.
confirmed.fix: Give Q18 its own NoulCriteriaSpec: true = the script fails now for the reason the issue describes AND its assertion states only what the issue promises (issue_quote), so it completes once that behaviour is fixed (examples: an assert on the value the issue says should be returned; a call the issue says must not raise); false = raises for another reason, asserts a detail the issue does not state (exact message text, repr formatting, ordering), or would keep failing after the described fix (≥ 2 examples each). confirmed.title: LLM phase waits for the whole round to close (slowest sample / deadline), not for the first passer; first-round deadline is 20 s because probe p90 is never wired
confirmed.scenario: runLlmStreaming awaits deps.runQueue whose worker loops on queue.next() (sieve/runner.ts:715, oracle/verify.ts:243) until feed() closes the queue after round.next() returns null (subgoal.ts:1209), i.e. after every sample settled. No rule stops on a plausible passer (stopDispatch only checks passers >= 5, runs, wall). collectForRank (subgoal.ts:1131/1166) and bestGuessPhases' `await llmRest` (round.rest()) have the same shape. sampleDeadlineMs (llm/source.ts:80) returns LLM_SAMPLE_DEADLINE.maxMs = 20 000 ms for the first round whenever probeP90Ms is null, and neither cli/session.ts:700 nor bench/runner.ts:558 passes `llm.probeP90Ms`, so on QuixBugs (2 steps/task, one LlmSource per run) effectively every LLM-needed round runs at the 20 s deadline. Concrete: QuixBugs program, seeds miss at site 1 (3.8 s) -> samples 1..3 released; sample 1 lands at 6 s with the correct patch, passes goal subset + full suite by ~8 s; sample 3 straggles (GLM p90 24-37 s) -> the queue stays open until the 20 s deadline from release -> decideBatch runs at ~24 s -> step wall ~25-34 s (with L1' adding another 10-20 s deadline + runs, worst ~70-80 s bounded by QUIXBUGS_TEST_WALL_MAX_MS 90 s) against §7.3's 10-14 s p50 / 21-24 s p90. verdict.reason: CONFIRMED. `writeReproduction` (src/synth/llm/repro.ts:335) awaits `Promise.all` over the 3 `write_reproduction` samples (bounded by REPRO_DEADLINE_MS 20 s), then iterates `for (const t of trials)` and, inside that loop, `await runRepro(...)` for the first base run (repro.ts:362) and `await runRepro(...)` again for the confirmation run (repro.ts:386) — strictly sequential, no Promise.all, no lane pool. `runRepro` (src/synth/oracle/runner.ts:336) is exactly one `run(command, {cwd, timeoutMs})` call with `timeoutMs = opts.timeoutMs ?? REPRO_TIMEOUT_MS` (30_000 at runner.ts:30); the caller `writeReproductionL2` (src/synth/search/index.ts:1343) passes no `timeoutMs`, so each of up to 6 runs may take 30 s. The call sits on the step-1 critical path with nothing overlapping it: `rebaselineRepository` awaits `initRepository` (index.ts:1172); `initRepository` awaits `findOracle`, then `writeReproductionL2` (index.ts:1273), then `locate`, then `regressionScope`; only after it returns does `fireEarlyRound` (the L1 fire, index.ts:1177) and the scoped-baseline `runTests` start. That matches the §7.1 order the design states (LLM-JEV-DESIGN.md:289) — the baseline cannot overlap the oracle. The design budgets this stage as "L2 ≤ 20 s + 2 base runs when needed" (§7.4, LLM-JEV-DESIGN.md:310; also §4c line 83), and §4.10 says each script runs "twice at base"; as a wall-time term "2 base runs" only holds if the three scripts' runs overlap, whereas the code does up to 3 × 2 = 6 serial runs. A timing reproduction against the real function (fake `run` delaying 150 ms, three distinct accepted scripts each raising at base) gave: 6 base runs, max concurrency 1, each run starting only after the previous ended, wall 909 ms ≈ 6 × 150 ms (vs ~300 ms if the three scripts ran concurrently). The fix is feasible: `sandboxRunFn` (src/synth/verify/index.ts:118) is a pass-through and `createSandbox().run` (src/sandbox/run.ts:238) spawns directly with no queue or lock, and the sieve runner already runs `oracle.lanes` candidates concurrently through the same sandbox. Two nuances on the finding as written: (a) magnitude — no llm-jev run on a repository-class instance exists in the checked-in bench results (the llm-jev dirs are ladder/quixbugs/smoke), so "6–8 s per Django run → 42 s" is a projection from the design's own per-run figures (§7.4 header "repro 1–3 s"; oracle/search.ts:356 "≈ 0.4–6.5 s" per confirmation run), giving 6–39 s serial vs 2–13 s overlapped by the design's numbers, with the 6 × 30 s = 180 s hang bound correct as stated; (b) fix detail — `mem.oracle.lanes` is computed by `laneCount` in `rebaselineRepository` after `initRepository` returns, so it is not available at L2 time; a fixed bound (REPRO_SAMPLES = 3) suffices, and separate worktrees are unnecessary because the harness writes nothing to disk (script travels base64 in the command) and Django gets a per-process in-memory sqlite. Severity medium is appropriate: a plan-conformance/latency defect on 21/30 SWE instances (§4.10), not a correctness bug.

rejected.title: jev-only behaviour changed without a mode gate: the full-suite passer cap is now per step (RunnerMemory.passersThisStep) in every mode, not just llm-jev
rejected.reason: The code does what the finding describes at the surface (src/synth/search/index.ts:552 resets `mem.passersThisStep = 0` in every mode; runner.ts:526 and verify.ts:199 seed the counter from it), but the finding fails on three counts. (1) The stated failure mechanism does not occur: `stopDispatch()` (runner.ts:541-542) is evaluated in the worker's `while` guard before `queue.pop` (runner.ts:731-737), so with the counter already at 5 the second call of the step dispatches nothing — the site-2 gold job is never popped, applied, or subset-charged, and never reaches the `defer` at runner.ts:671 or `mem.deferred`; a /tmp reproduction (/tmp/jevrepro-passers/cap.test.ts) confirms `[]` returned, queue size unchanged, subset-run count unchanged, `testRunsLeft` unchanged, `mem.deferred` empty, then `plausible` after the next-step reset. The unpopped job is carried by the search queue (src/synth/sieve/queue.ts:37 carryOver) and the source is not marked exhausted (subgoal.ts:865-866, `completed` false), so the only effect is the one-step delay. (2) "Without a mode gate" is a documented decision, not an oversight: docs/DECISIONS.md:670-681 "The full-suite passer cap is per step in every mode" names exactly this jev-only consequence, states runner.ts:73 said "per step" all along (the per-call local was the deviation), and explicitly rejects a per-mode switch; docs/DESIGN.md:3098-3099 (§22.5) records it; test/unit/synth/sieve/runner.test.ts:539-557 asserts the per-step semantics and the suite is green (52/52). (3) The bench claim is wrong as written: docs/LLM-JEV-DESIGN.md §10.1 says "The checked-in jev-only finals are the no-generator reference (not re-run)" and the head-to-head baseline for criteria 1-4 is jev-off; the llm-jev result dirs (bench/results/llm-jev-{smoke,quixbugs,ladder}/summary.json) contain only the `llm-jev` condition, so there is no jev-only arm being measured against. The one true residue — the stored jev-only reference rows were produced under the per-call rule and could differ by a step where >5 passers across sites all regress — is the tradeoff DECISIONS 2026-09-21 accepts, a bench-procedure note rather than a code defect, and the stored records (tasks.jsonl) carry no per-step verify counts to quantify it.
